record.paper_title: Minimal positive realizations: a survey of recent results and open problems
record.original_question: For the minimality problem for positive realizations of a strictly proper rational transfer function G(z), which extra eigenvalues must sometimes be introduced in a smallest-dimensional positive realization even though they are not present in the original minimal realization? In other words, can one fully characterize the "hidden modes" that may need to be added in order to obtain a minimal positive realization?

evidence.quote: The positive realization problem consists of providing answers to the questions: - (The minimality problem) What is a minimal value for N?

Another important issue related to minimality of positive systems is the study of "hidden modes", i.e. of the eigenvalues which possibly one has to add in order to obtain a minimal positive realization.
A full characterization of this property may lead to a deeper and valuable insight into the problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G(z)$ be a strictly proper rational transfer function with nonnegative impulse response, i.e., the formal expansion $G(z)=\sum_{k\ge 1} g_k z^{-k}$ satisfies $g_k\ge 0$ for all $k\ge 1$. A positive realization of $G(z)$ of dimension $N$ is a triple $(A,b,c)$ with $A\in\mathbb{R}_+^{N	imes N}$, $b\in\mathbb{R}_+^{N}$, $c\in\mathbb{R}_+^{1	imes N}$ (entrywise nonnegative) such that $G(z)=c(zI-A)^{-1}b$. A positive realization is called minimal if $N$ is the smallest possible dimension, denoted $N_+(G)$. Let $n$ denote the McMillan degree of $G$ (the dimension of a minimal, not necessarily positive, realization), and let $\sigma(G)$ denote the set of poles of $G$ (counted with multiplicity).

In general $N_+(G)\ge n$, and a minimal positive realization $(A,b,c)$ of $G$ may have spectrum $\sigma(A)$ strictly larger than $\sigma(G)$; the extra eigenvalues in $\sigma(A)\setminus\sigma(G)$ are called hidden modes.

Problem. Give a complete characterization, in terms of $G(z)$ (equivalently, in terms of $\sigma(G)$ and the nonnegative sequence $\{g_k\}$), of which multisets of complex numbers can or must appear as the multiset of hidden modes $\sigma(A)\setminus\sigma(G)$ of some (equivalently, of every) minimal positive realization of $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers on minimal positive realizations (including a 2022 Automatica survey and works on two-pole transfer functions) indicate that a complete characterization of the hidden modes required in a minimal positive realization remains an open problem; only partial results exist for special cases such as low McMillan degree or specific pole configurations.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive realizations: A survey (Automatica, 2022)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of recent results on minimal positive realizations, noting that general characterization of minimality remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Characterizing minimality (and the associated hidden modes) of positive realizations is still an open problem in general.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive realizations for linear systems with two-different-pole transfer functions
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes minimal positive realization results in the restricted setting of two distinct poles.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial/special-case characterizations of minimal positive realizations and their hidden modes are known.

status_evidence.title: Positive systems in the state space approach: main issues and recent results
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open issues including the minimality problem and hidden eigenvalues for positive realizations.
status_evidence.claim: The hidden-mode characterization for minimal positive realizations is listed among open issues.
